pr_body:
What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

What this PR does / why we need it:
Fix cacheWatcher leak when time jump to the future and jump back

Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
#96259

```release-note
Fix memory leak in kube-apiserver when underlying time goes forth and back.
```

issue_context.title: kube-apiserver will leak cacheWatcher  when time jump to the future and jump back
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

kube-apiserver will leak cacheWatcher when time jump to the future and jump back。

In telecom application scenarios, We expect kubernetes to work properly when time changes.

It is found that when the time of the node where kube-apiserver resides changes to the future for several minutes and change back, memory leak occurs on kube-apiserver.

before time change
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1468240/98235618-05a5a380-1f9d-11eb-8615-5feb1a47ac2e.png)

change time to future then change back, wait 1 hour
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1468240/98235628-08a09400-1f9d-11eb-9c4e-7e053ed8efdc.png)

**What you expected to happen**:

kubernetes to work properly when time changes, no memroy leak

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. change the time of the node where kube-apiserver resides to the future (for example, one day),
2. wait several minutes 
3. change time back

**Anything else we need to know?**:
I confirmed the code in v1.19 and the problem exists.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):1.15.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): EulerOS 2.0
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux 4.19.36
- Install tools: 
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments: @chenyw1990 - so are you saying that the time can go forth and back without the components (in this case kube-apiserver) being even restarted? Can you briefly describe how that happens?

> change the time of the node where kube-apiserver resides to the future (for example, one day),

Can it really change by one day? If you repro-ed it by changing by one day, the memory will free-up after that one day actually...

That's not entirely true - they will be GC-ed once we reach the previous time. So unless it won't jump by hours, but rather minutes/seconds, you won't leak the memory.
How much it can change? I would like to avoid non-trivial logic if it's not absolutely needed.

@wojtek-t 

we test in 2000 nodes cluster，When the cluster runs stably，before cacheWatcher leak，the memory used by kube-apiserver is 14 GB.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1468240/98537738-ae694100-22c4-11eb-91da-5ef0ed7e30fc.png)

when cacheWatcher leak， the memory usage increases to 43.85 GB after 4.5 hours, and about 6.6 GB memory is leaked every hour.
![aftermemoryleak](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1468240/98538182-5717a080-22c5-11eb-8226-b06934915305.png)

If some applications are being installed, or nodes are being joined in batches，memory leaks faster

so, if the time changes by hour, the memory leakage problem is serious.

The fix was merged at head.

I also opened cherrypicks - they are waiting for approval.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96601
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96602
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96603

Closing since there is nothing else left to do here.

review_comments: Going back to my original comment about adding a test - can't you use FakeClock to test this?

The essence of this problem is that the display clock changes, but the mononotonic clock does not change.
The FakeClock time can be changed using either of the following methods: SetTime and Step, both methods change FakeClock.time. The display clock and monotonic clock change simultaneously. Therefore, the problem cannot be simulated.

OK - that sounds reasonable.

@liggitt - do you have any suggestions what else can we do here? Or can we go with as is?
I also don't see a way to exercise the bug with the new code, so I'd be happy with this fix as is
